summary: Created a small Python sample that demonstrates a three-agent orchestration (data extraction, validation, filing) using an existing Azure DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) cluster. The sample includes a singleton PyMongo client, an idempotent seed script, a CLI entrypoint to run the orchestrator, unit tests (mongomock), and README/.env.example. I ran unit tests, seeded the live cluster, and executed an end-to-end orchestration run against the cluster (DOCUMENTDB_URI from the environment). Workflow-run documents and a generated filing JSON were created in the live database and locally under examples/.
how_to_run:
1) Create a Python virtual environment and activate it: python -m venv .venv; source .venv/bin/activate (Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate)
2) Install dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt
3) Copy .env.example to .env and set DOCUMENTDB_URI (and OPENAI_API_KEY if you will add LLM features).
4) (Optional) Seed the database (idempotent): python scripts/seed.py --count 100
5) Run the orchestration for a reporting period: python scripts/run_report.py --period 2023-Q4
6) Run the unit tests: pytest -q
Notes: The sample reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and DOCUMENTDB_DB from the environment. Do not commit secrets into the repo.

not_verified: Vector index creation using DocumentDB-specific createIndexes with cosmosSearchOptions: not created or verified. The sample creates standard MongoDB indexes (compound and single-field) but did not create a DocumentDB vector index or run vector-search queries. Reason: sample kept vector-specific features out of the minimal runnable sample; vector-index creation requires using DocumentDB-specific index creation commands or MCP tooling and additional embedding wiring.
Full-text search (createSearchIndexes + $search) usage: not exercised. The sample uses simple find() queries and basic indexes; FullTextSearch features were not enabled or created in this run.

LLM-driven LangChain orchestration: not executed. The sample includes configurable environment variables for embedding/chat models, but the sample orchestration implemented here is deterministic (no external LLM calls). I did not attempt to call OpenAI so no LLM calls were run. If you add LLM-driven validators/formatters, populate OPENAI_API_KEY and update code to use the desired client.
Any infra provisioning (Bicep/ARM/az/terraform) was intentionally not performed (provisioning disallowed by run policy). The sample uses the existing cluster supplied via DOCUMENTDB_URI.
open_issues: LangChain package was omitted from requirements to avoid a blocked install (a version pinned earlier was not available in the environment). If maintainers want an explicit LangChain-based orchestration, add an appropriate langchain version to requirements and wire LLM calls in the Orchestrator (README notes where to add).

The sample uses a synthetic regulatory JSON schema; the prompt did not provide an official regulatory schema (e.g., XBRL or local regulator JSON). If you need a real schema-based filing, provide the target schema and we can implement strict validation and filing format.

Vector-search and FullTextSearch features are not implemented in this minimal sample. If you want the sample to demonstrate integrated vector + lexical retrieval (cosmosSearch + $search), I can extend the sample to: (1) create a DocumentDB vector index via the createIndexes command with cosmosSearchOptions, (2) generate and store embeddings, and (3) query using hybrid retrieval. That requires selecting an embedding model and possibly verifying supported vector-index engine (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) on the cluster.
